subject: microbiology
title: Cestode Cobalamin Deficiency, Hymenolepis nana and Schistosoma

steps.tx: A classic metabolic consequence of high-burden Diphyllobothrium latum infection in the proximal jejunum is severe **vitamin B12 deficiency**. The adult tapeworm possesses high affinity for intrinsic factor-cobalamin complexes, absorbing up to one hundred percent of ingested dietary vitamin B12. This nutritional theft starves the host of cobalamin, precipitating macrocytic megaloblastic anaemia identical to pernicious anaemia.
steps.say: The fish tapeworm absorbs dietary cobalamin in the jejunum, producing severe megaloblastic anaemia.

steps.tx: Neurological consequences of long-standing tapeworm-induced cobalamin deficiency mirror subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord. Demyelination of the posterior and lateral columns produces progressive sensory ataxia, loss of vibration and position sense, spastic paraparesis, and positive Babinski signs. Oral **praziquantel** rapidly expels the worm, after which parenteral cyanocobalamin supplementation restores haematological parameters.
steps.say: Spinal cord posterior column demyelination causes sensory ataxia; single-dose praziquantel cures the infestation.

nodes.label: Adult tapeworm in jejunum sequesters ingested vitamin B12

steps.tx: The dwarf tapeworm **Hymenolepis nana** is the smallest tapeworm infecting humans, measuring only one to four centimetres in length, and is the most common cestode worldwide. It possesses the unique biological capability among cestodes of completing its entire life cycle within a single human host without requiring an obligate intermediate host, predisposing to intense autoinfection.
steps.say: Dwarf tapeworm completes its entire life cycle in one host, making internal autoinfection possible.

vis.caption: Comparative cestode morphology illustrating Hymenolepis nana life cycle and egg anatomy [Credit: CDC, StewardMD cleared]

steps.tx: When ingested, H. nana eggs hatch in the duodenum, where hexacanth oncospheres penetrate villi to become cysticercoids before re-entering the intestinal lumen to mature into adult worms. In internal autoinfection, eggs hatch inside the bowel without ever leaving the host, producing heavy worm burdens of thousands of tapeworms. Stool microscopy reveals spherical, colorless eggs with an inner membrane bearing two **polar filaments** emerging from polar knobs.
steps.say: Spherical colorless eggs show two polar knobs with four to eight wavy polar filaments.

steps.tx: Blood flukes belonging to the genus Schistosoma reside as paired copulating adults within human visceral venous plexuses. Infection occurs when free-swimming fork-tailed cercariae shed by aquatic snail hosts penetrate intact skin during freshwater bathing. Adult **Schistosoma haematobium** pairs migrate to the vesical and pelvic venous plexuses draining the urinary bladder.
steps.say: Aquatic cercariae penetrate skin; adult haematobium pairs migrate to the vesical venous plexus.

nodes.label: Free-swimming cercariae shed by Bulinus snails penetrate human skin
Schistosomulae migrate via lungs and liver into vesical venous plexus
Paired adults oviposit eggs that penetrate through bladder wall into urine

steps.tx: Females oviposit hundreds of large, elongated, non-operculated eggs bearing a prominent, sharp **terminal spine**. As eggs traverse the bladder mucosal wall, they induce granulomatous inflammation, ulceration, and painless terminal haematuria. Chronic fibrosis produces calcified bladder walls appearing as an eggshell bladder on pelvic radiography, obstructive hydronephrosis, and markedly increased risk of squamous cell carcinoma of the urinary bladder.
steps.say: Sharp terminal-spined eggs erode the bladder mucosa, causing painless haematuria and squamous cell carcinoma.

rows: Egg extrusion through inflamed mucosal venules
Painless blood at the end of micturition
Deposition of calcium in dead mural eggs
Curvilinear eggshell calcification on pelvic radiograph
Large oval egg with sharp pointed terminal spine

steps.tx: In contrast, adult pairs of **Schistosoma mansoni** reside in the inferior mesenteric venules draining the large intestine, while Schistosoma japonicum occupies the superior mesenteric venules. S. mansoni eggs possess a prominent, large, sharp lateral spine, whereas S. japonicum eggs are rounded with a rudimentary, inconspicuous lateral knob or spine.
steps.say: Mansoni eggs feature a large sharp lateral spine and migrate through the wall of the colon.

left.title: Schistosoma mansoni
points: Egg morphology: prominent sharp lateral spine

right.title: Schistosoma japonicum
points: Egg morphology: rounded with small lateral knob

steps.tx: Eggs carried retrogradely in the portal venous flow lodge within intrahepatic portal venules, provoking T-cell-mediated granulomatous inflammation. Fibrotic healing produces pathognomonic **Symmers pipestem fibrosis**, where dense white fibrous bands encircle portal tracts without altering lobular architecture. This non-cirrhotic presinusoidal portal hypertension produces massive splenomegaly and life-threatening bleeding from oesophageal varices.
steps.say: Embolized eggs induce Symmers pipestem periportal fibrosis, driving severe presinusoidal portal hypertension.

nodes.label: Oviposited eggs carried retrogradely into intrahepatic portal venules
